There were 57 contested State Representative and State Senate seats in
the November 3, 2026, Massachusetts general election. We published a
[forecast for these races](/posts/2026-10-29-contested-races/), which
was based on our
[legislative model](https://bwbensonjr.github.io/election-modeling/)
that is trained on legislative elections from 2010 through 2024. We
will look at the races we expected to be the most competitive,
consider a notable upset, present the complete results, and look at
how the results compared to the model in aggregate.

## Results of the four closest forecast races

The races that looked to be the most competitive according to the
model featured three Republican incumbents and one Democratic
incumbent, all in swing districts. Two of the incumbents, Marcus
Vaughn (R-Wrentham) and Donald Wong (R-Saugus), survived their
challenges, while Steven Ouellette (D-Westport) and David Vieira
(R-Falmouth) were defeated.

```{r top-four-results}
#| column: page
featured |>
    with_provisional_outcomes() |>
    results_table("", show_margin_note = FALSE) |>
    cols_label(opponent = "Republican") |>
    cols_hide(columns = other_votes) |>
    tab_options(table.width = px(885))
```

### 9th Norfolk

```{r 9th-norfolk-results-map, fig.height=6}
municipality_result_map("Ninth Norfolk")
```
<br/>
State Representative Marcus Vaughn (R-Wrentham) slightly outperformed
the model's central forecast of a 1.8-point GOP win
by finishing 4.7 points ahead of challenger Thomas Melville
(D-Medfield), keeping this longtime Republican seat. The seat was
previously held by Shawn Dooley (R-Norfolk), Richard Ross
(R-Wrentham), and Scott Brown (R-Wrentham), who went on to serve in
both the Massachusetts Senate and the U.S. Senate.

### 8th Bristol

```{r 8th-bristol-results-map, fig.height=6}
municipality_result_map("Eighth Bristol")
```
<br/>
The 8th Bristol State Representative district, with towns straddling
Fall River and New Bedford, will have a Republican representative in
Jesse St. Gelais (R-Acushnet) after being in Democratic hands for more
than half a century. St. Gelais outperformed the forecast's D+2.2
Democratic margin by almost five points for an R+2.6 win over first-term
incumbent State Representative Steven Ouellette
(D-Westport). Ouellette won his hometown of Westport and the
district's three precincts of Fall River, while St. Gelais won the
district's precincts of Freetown, Acushnet, and New Bedford.

### 9th Essex

```{r 9th-essex-results-map, fig.height=6}
municipality_result_map("Ninth Essex")
```
<br/>
The model saw State Representative Donald Wong (R-Saugus) as a
2.6-point favorite over challenger Peter Meaney (D-Lynn) in the North
Shore's 9th Essex district. Wong won by a ten-point margin to earn a
ninth term by running up a 22-point margin in Saugus and winning by 2
points in Wakefield. Meaney won the two precincts of Lynn by about 7
points. Wong was first elected State Representative in the red wave of 2010.

### 3rd Barnstable

```{r 3rd-barnstable-results-map, fig.height=6}
municipality_result_map("Third Barnstable")
```
<br/>
The other incumbent from our focus group to lose his seat on Tuesday
was David Vieira (R-Falmouth), another Republican who was also first
elected as State Representative 16 years ago in 2010. Jack Richardson
(D-Falmouth) pushed things just over the model's projection of a
2.8-point Democratic margin to a 3.5-point victory. Richardson was
able to outraise and outspend Vieira, often a difficult accomplishment
for a challenger.

## Tuesday's biggest surprise: The 22nd Middlesex

State Representative Marc Lombardo (R-Billerica), like Vieira and Wong,
was elected in the 2010 red wave and has earned a reputation as one of
Massachusetts's most conservative legislators. The model predicted an
almost 15-point victory for Lombardo against his Democratic challenger
based on his incumbency, the presidential voting history of the
district, and his fundraising advantage.

The biggest surprise from the legislative elections on Tuesday ended up
being 19-year-old Daniel Darris-O'Connor (D-Billerica) and his 2.5-point
victory over incumbent Lombardo. Darris-O'Connor is a sitting
member of the Billerica select board and
[will assume office the day after his 20th birthday in January](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/11/04/metro/darris-oconnor-lombardo-billerica-legislature/).

```{r notable-results}
#| column: page
results_table(notable, "", show_margin_note = FALSE) |>
    cols_hide(columns = other_votes) |>
    tab_options(table.width = px(885))
```

```{r 22nd-middlesex-results-map, fig.height=6}
municipality_result_map("Twenty-Second Middlesex") +
    tm_view(set_view = 12)
```
<br/>

The 22nd Middlesex district is one of four Massachusetts State
Representative districts that consist of a single, wholly contained
municipality. The other three are the 4th Worcester (Leominster), 2nd
Berkshire (Pittsfield), and 7th Essex (Salem).

## Results for all contested seats

Of the 57 contested State Representative and State Senate seats, eight
were open seats with no incumbent running and 49 were incumbent
challenges. Three of the 49 incumbents were defeated, and a fourth
trails in the uncalled 2nd Plymouth race.

```{r outcome-summary}
outcome_summary_table(results)
```

In terms of party, 39 of the 57 contested seats were
Democratic-held seats that stayed Democratic. Democrats won four
Republican-held seats and lead in a fifth, the uncalled 2nd Plymouth
race. One Democratic-held seat was won by a Republican (St. Gelais
over Ouellette in the 8th Bristol), and 12 Republican-held seats were
held by the GOP.

```{r statewide-results-map}
#| column: body-outset
statewide_outcome_map()
```

### Results of all 57 contested legislative races

The table of districts and outcomes is sorted by the size of
Democratic or Republican over- or under-performance compared to the
model, which can also be thought of as model error.

It is notable that the biggest differences from the model's
predictions were instances of Democratic over-performance against a
non-Republican candidate. We have seen that races between Democrats
and non-Republican opponents are harder for the model to predict, with
testing on Dem/non-GOP races showing an absolute error of about 15
points, compared with 8 points for Dem/GOP matchups. In addition, the
model tends to underestimate Democratic margins in Dem/non-GOP
races. The 2026 results follow that same pattern.

```{r all-results}
#| column: screen
results |>
    with_provisional_outcomes() |>
    arrange(desc(abs(signed_error)), chamber, district_display) |>
    results_table("", full = TRUE)
```

## Results compared to model forecast

All but six of the race outcomes fall within the model's 75%
predictive intervals. Each interval represents the range in which the
model placed a 75% probability of that race's result falling.

Four of the six outliers are instances of a Democrat facing a
non-Republican. One of the other two outliers is the uncalled 2nd
Plymouth race where challenger Sarah Hewins (D-Carver) seems to be
significantly outperforming the R+15.8 model forecast against
incumbent John Gaskey (R-Carver) with an 89-vote lead.

The remaining outlier is the 22nd Middlesex win by 19-year-old Daniel
Darris-O'Connor (D-Billerica) over incumbent Marc Lombardo
(R-Billerica).

```{r forecast-performance}
#| column: body-outset
#| results: asis

```
